Started as a studio space for Banele to create and represent himself from, BKhz (the gallery) came to be when Banele acted on his desire to grant his contemporaries access to an exhibition space that would prioritise their holistic well-being as best as possible. The gallery continues to operate by the ethos of putting the needs, wants, and vision of the artist first. Since its opening in August 2018, BKhz Gallery has hosted numerous group and solo exhibitions, showing works by emerging and established artists, in South Africa and abroad. The team at BKhz works with intentions to better impact the gallery’s immediate community through: diversity in the selection of artists, deliberately foregrounding women artists, increasing the ease of accessibility to audiences, and providing visual and academic discourse.

item.title: Jonathan Ball Publishers
item.description: Jonathan Ball Publishers is one of South Africa’s leading publishing houses, founded in 1976. The company is renowned for publishing a wide range of high-quality works, including non-fiction, politics, history, current affairs, and fiction by prominent South African and international authors. With a commitment to fostering strong local voices and bringing global perspectives to South African readers, Jonathan Ball Publishers has played a key role in shaping the country’s literary and intellectual landscape.

item.title: Picha
item.description: Picha and the Lubumbashi Biennale Founded in 2008 in Lubumbashi, the Picha Collective emerged from the initiative of a group of artists and cultural practitioners seeking to create a space for reflection, production, and dissemination dedicated to contemporary art in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The word Picha, meaning “image” in Swahili, reflects the collective’s ambition to use art and visual expression as tools for storytelling, memory, and dialogue. Since its inception, Picha has aimed to build a sustainable cultural ecosystem in the DRC by supporting local talent and fostering connections with artistic communities across Africa and beyond. To achieve this vision, Picha is structured around three key pillars: • The Picha Art and Research Center, located in Makomeno — a dynamic space for exhibitions, creation, and artistic exchange; • The Picha Workshops, a training and mentorship program designed to support emerging artists; • The Lubumbashi Biennale, the organization’s flagship event dedicated to lens- based and contemporary art practices. The Lubumbashi Biennale, formerly known as Rencontres Picha, has become one of the most significant events in contemporary art across Central Africa. Held every two years, it brings together artists, curators, and researchers from around the world around themes that question the city, its history, and its transformations. Over the years, the Biennale has helped establish Lubumbashi as a vibrant artistic hub, where creation, critical thought, and engagement converge. Its upcoming edition in 2026 will further affirm Picha and the Lubumbashi Biennale as key platforms for Congolese and African contemporary art, deeply rooted locally yet open to the world. Collective: Sammy Baloji (founder), George Senga, Filip De Boeck, Gabriele Salmi, Aimé Kalenda, Jean Katambayi (president), Alexandre Mulongo, Rosa Spaliviero Coordinator: Jean-Sylvain Tshilumba Director: Gaelle Van Lede

item.title: Siwa Mgoboza
item.description: Siwa Mgoboza is an award-winning artist, curator, and cultural entrepreneur, who contributes an incisive international perspective shaped by engagements with the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art and the South African Pavilion at the 60th Venice Biennale di Arte 2024. Their practice bridges diasporic, queer, and decolonial discourses. Mgoboza sits on the SOHO HOUSE South Africa Selection Committee and is a board member at Banana Art Club Residency Program in Botswana.

item.title: Timika Sukhai
item.description: Timika Sukhai is a South African–born writer, researcher, and emerging curator whose interdisciplinary practice engages critically with archival histories, Indigenous knowledge systems, and creative storytelling. Over the past four years living in Scotland, she has developed a distinctive research and creative practice grounded in postcolonial inquiry, experimental methodologies, and the reimagining of historical narratives. This period has allowed her to refine her approach to working with cultural archives, deepen her engagement with community-focused heritage work, and expand her commitment to accessible, dialogic forms of curation. Working fluidly across research, writing, and curatorial experimentation, Timika interrogates how colonial archives have shaped, and often distorted, representations of Indigenous and marginalized communities. She approaches the archive as a living, contested, and relational space, employing creative methods that challenge dominant historical frameworks while foregrounding resilience, continuity, and lived experience. Central to her practice is an ethics of care, advocacy, and community-led engagement, ensuring that historical material is not only examined critically but activated in ways that invite participation, reflection, and reclamation. Her ongoing body of work, Beyond Barbarians, explores the language of empire and its enduring impact on Indigenous identity, land, and belonging. Spanning hybrid writing, curatorial workshops, and proposed exhibition formats, the project seeks to create meaningful encounters between archival material and contemporary interpretation. Alongside her creative and research practice, Timika is committed to public engagement within cultural and heritage spaces. Through exhibitions, collaborative initiatives, and narrative-driven research, she aims to reframe historical memory, amplify marginalized voices, and position storytelling as a vital act of cultural resistance and restoration.

item.title: Tommaso Fiscaletti
item.description: Tommaso Fiscaletti (1981) is a photographic artist based in Cape Town. His work explores the connection between humans, memory, and the universe, moving between reality and imagination. In 2016, his project Between Home and Wisdom was presented in a wide exhibition at the Santa Maria Della Scala Museum in Siena, accompanied by a monograph. The same year, he began working with Nic Grobler on Hemelliggaam or The Attempt To Be Here Now (Hemelliggaam, in Afrikaans: heavenly body), a visual archive of photographs, videos, and installations that brings together images of astronomical observatories, remote landscapes, and inspirations from old local (Afrikaans) science fiction novels. The project, which took six years to complete, has been exhibited in various South African museums, including the Iziko South African Museum in Cape Town and the Pretoria Art Museum. Today, this exploration is evolving into a book. In 2021, he began collaborating with anthropologist Nicola Perugini on The Skin Underneath. Through photography and public installations, the project examines how citizens perceive the Villa Marina Colony, a Fascist-era building on the Pesaro waterfront (the author's hometown), shedding light on individual and collective stories. His works are part of public and private collections and have been showcased internationally. Fiscaletti has taught photography at IED Milan and currently teaches at the Creative Academy in Cape Town.

item.title: Puleng Mongale
item.description: Puleng Mongale (b. 1991) is a contemporary visual artist based in Durban, South Africa, specialising in photography and digital media. Since the inception of her art practice, Mongale has used her creative expression to probe into her subconscious to process and articulate her lived experiences. Over the years, her artistic journey has evolved into a reflective exploration of themes that resonate with her as a young African woman in South Africa. Mongale’s work explores themes related to spirituality, belonging, identity, and womanhood. Mongale’s work has been shown in multiple group exhibitions including Africa Foto Fair, Abidjan (2023); Abadali Group Show, Johannesburg (2022); The Fold Group Show, London (2021); Beyond Group Show, Cologne (2021); Terrains of Possibility at the Rele Gallery in Lagos (2021); Heaven on Earth, an online solo exhibition with Doyle Wham x Latitudes (2021); and Ambiguous, a group exhibition with mmArthouse (2020). In an ever-evolving society, art serves as Mongale's resistance, a tool to define her narrative on her terms.

item.title: Kalashnikovv Gallery
item.description: Kalashnikovv Gallery was founded in 2013 in direct response to the traditional white cube gallery system by envisioning an alternative operational model for the visual arts. It is administered and curated by two of Johannesburg's deep-rooted cultural instigators, M.J Turpin and Matthew Dean Dowdle who prioritize a collaborative exchange in working with the artists they partner with. Kalashnikovv currently represents a range of artists with emerging to established careers. The gallery and its staff work in conversation with these artists to build networks, exposure and foster personal growth through exhibitions, residencies and exchanges. The gallery is both a commercial art space as well as a project space for experimentation with an ethos of socio-political engagement and accessibility. This sentiment operates at all levels of the gallery structure in order to facilitate new benchmarks of value for artists, collectors and visitors from within, and outside of, the existing art ecosystem. Kalashnikovv is a South African based gallery that is constantly expanding its scope to partner with creators and communities across the world. These interactions with local and international networks continually help to deconstruct and interrogate the idea of what a contemporary art platform can be in order to facilitate the changing role of art in modern society.

item.title: KZNSA Gallery
item.description: KwaZulu-Natal Society of Arts (KZNSA) is the leading contemporary art gallery in the province, offering cutting-edge art exhibitions and cultural events to the public for free. Established in 1902 and based in Durban, South Africa, KZNSA transforms the local arts community through activating and incubating contemporary ideas, artists, and cultural production. This is primarily achieved through exhibitions, artist-led educational initiatives, an annual members' competition, as well as retail partnership opportunities for artists. Representation at art fairs of KZN artists facilitates their exposure to the industry and career growth. KZNSA is a member-based society, registered Public Benefit Organisation and Non Profit Organisation, with 18A status. Gallery Website | Instagram | Facebook

item.title: No End Contemporary
item.description: Established in 2015, No End Contemporary Art Space is an artist-run contemporary art gallery situated in Linden (JHB). The gallery was started by Maaike Bakker, Jayne Crawshay-Hall and Dalene Victor Meyer in 2015. NO END Contemporary aims to showcase work in a variety of media by contemporary artists working and living in South Africa. No End Contemporary's main objective is to support young artists and curators by providing a platform to showcase their work. No End Contemporary also sets out to expand on the art-buyer pool by encouraging both established and emerging buyers to invest in successful art pieces in order to assist in creating a more self sustainable contemporary art cycle. Gallery Website | Instagram | Facebook

item.title: Thenga Art
item.description: 'Thenga' a Zulu word meaning; to buy, to sell, or to shop. This is marketplace, a meeting place, a home for those with passion, interest and love for African art. Based within the cultural milieu of Durban, South Africa, where the emerging local talent is vibrant and tenacious, our mission is to identify and expose this talent to growth opportunities through the Thenga market place. Thenga is a global online art shop, not gallery, our art is for everyone not just collectors. We sell art that changes lives, art that awakens imaginations and transforms people’s homes. In a world where everyone wants to ‘commercialise’ and ‘industrialise’ Thenga is unique, our focus is on the original, hand crafted, one of a kind pieces each with a heart, soul and story of their own. The Thenga team is dedicated to exploring diverse locations to discover artistic talent that hasn’t yet had the opportunity to rise up into the commercial world of art. We facilitates emerging and mid-career artists enabling them to make a living doing what they love. Thenga is a safe, mutually beneficial environment designed to give artists a large platform in which to sell their art and for international buyers to shop with confidence. Thenga has been guiding, mentoring and supporting local South African artists since 2014. Thenga.art is the next logical step to share our talented African artists and their hand crafted work with the rest of the world. The most important part of our business is building relationships with our artists and customers and we stand by our values of integrity and honesty in everything we do. Website

item.title: Creative Block By Spier Arts Trust
item.description: The Creative Block, now curated by Tamlin Blake, represents more than 260 professional artists from across South Africa. Each unique artwork is an expression of an individual artist's story, subject matter and style. When displayed together, they create a rich expression of contemporary South African culture. Creative Block by Spier Arts Trust | Instagram

item.title: Luamba Muinga
item.description: Luamba Muinga (Luanda, 1995) is a curator, producer, cultural critic and writer. Co-edited "Are we not makers of history?" (Bag Factory, Jorburg, 2020) with mozambican curator Sara Carneiro. Coordinates LabCC – Laboratório de Crítica e Curadoria, art platform for young curators and art critics from Luanda. His curatorial/cultural production (articles, reviews, essays, research) has been focused on permanence of memory, about how we appropriate the past, extracting its context, to locate it in the present. Personal narratives about the contemporary political history of Angola and its nuances in the post-war era. Angolan transition from communism to a capitalist-based policy and its nation-building projects. Urban dynamics as a space of conflict between colonial architecture and ours; and public spaces as a space for corporate power and intervention. Luamba is the coordinator of Don´t Waste, Create (2020, first edition), environmental art prize for Angoalissar company. He is co-founder of the art magazine Palavra&Arte and has published art articles/reviews in Cultura – Jornal Angolano de Arte e Letras. And hosts ART APPRECIATION, a program of events focused on author cinema and video art.

item.title: Tzung-Hui Lauren Lee
item.description: Tzung Hui Lauren Lee (b.1998) is a multimedia, South African Chinese artist currently based in Johannesburg. Lee has also recently completed her BA in Fine Arts from the Wits School of Arts at the University of the Witwatersrand. Her practice is predominantly installation-based and emerges through the processes within digital spaces, paper-making, sculpture and calligraphy. Lee’s process continues to evolve via the act of translating two-dimensional markings (her writings) to three-dimensional space. The artist draws inspiration from various aspects within Chinese philosophy and culture which include customary Chinese folk art where she investigates ideas pertaining to personal diaspora, decolonising the self, identity and relationships across and within the past and present. Lee’s work also forms part of the BMW Groups Private Art Collection (2021) situated at the BMW Midrand Campus, Johannesburg.
